tasks.short: Plan or execute nutrition and reproduction programmes

steps.what: Plan animal nutrition or reproduction programs from animal needs and veterinary evidence
Execute the chosen program, assess animal response and adjust within clinical authority

tasks.design: Use existing animal records in the veterinary clinical system {OTHER} and current guidance in {DOCS}. The veterinarian chooses the nutrition or reproduction programme and assesses implementation; no generic human-care calculation or model selects animal-specific interventions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme suitability depends on species, health, history and practical implementation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can support planning without replacing clinical programme decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Changing animal condition, uncertain response and constraints on feeding or breeding practice.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when a programme needs adjustment or further investigation.
tasks.altitude: Programme authority and clinical time stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Species-specific requirements and limits of standard feeding calculations

evidence.claim: The digest does not establish veterinary nutrition or reproduction programme automation; clinical planning and execution remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is veterinarian programme planning and clinical implementation/review, not routine feeding labour or a separate scheduling task. Nutrition and reproduction are alternative programme routes, not a single mandatory combined service.

No machine relies on assumed structured animal requirements, breeding readiness or safe ration fields. Original assessments are interpreted by the veterinarian with all planning and implementation time retained.

Use native animal records first. Zero upkeep because no new programme engine or integration is introduced. Animal-care team labour is outside this denominator and unchanged; national veterinary rules govern local practice.
unknowns: Programme types, species and division of clinical and routine care work
research_questions: Which programme calculations are distinct and repetitive enough to measure separately from clinical judgement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Planning40 and implementation/review60 retain full time; no assumed ration-entry or schedule baseline is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct postmortem examination and obtain relevant specimens and observations
Analyse postmortem findings and available tests to determine likely causes of death

tasks.design: Retain the physical postmortem and causal interpretation with the veterinarian, using existing case and laboratory records in {OTHER}. Guidance in {DOCS} supports the examination, but no model assigns a cause of death or substitutes for specimen work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cause of death requires integration of physical findings, history and sometimes laboratory evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing digital records support access without replacing examination or causal reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Decomposition, non-specific findings and distinguishing contributing conditions from the cause of death.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertainty and deciding which findings merit further testing.
tasks.altitude: Postmortem responsibility and time stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Specimen suitability and limits of causal inference

evidence.claim: Human-care imaging and documentation capabilities in the digest do not establish veterinary postmortem examination or cause-of-death automation.

assumptions: Boundary includes the veterinarian's examination and interpretation, not laboratory processing, transport or a separate final report. Tests are conditional; their producer is the laboratory's existing specimen workflow and its labour is excluded and unchanged.

Veterinarian produces specimen identity and postmortem observations in s1 with all65 hours retained. No machine consumes free lesion labels or inferred causes; absent test results remain unresolved rather than generated.
Native case access comes first. Zero upkeep because no new postmortem system is introduced; national animal-health procedures and referral requirements must be confirmed locally.
unknowns: National reporting or animal-health investigation requirements
research_questions: Which findings can support a cause-of-death assessment and which require further testing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Physical examination65 and causal assessment35 retain full time; no external laboratory saving enters the denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Maintain specialist knowledge through study, professional learning and case review
Apply and develop specialist treatment expertise through supervised or independent case practice

tasks.design: Use existing literature access in {DOCS} and learning records in {LMS}. Keep critical study and specialist case practice with the veterinarian; generated summaries do not establish competence, certification or a safe reduction in clinical learning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specialisation requires experience and critical understanding of a defined clinical field.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital learning access supports development without replacing professional competence.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing when new evidence is applicable and when a case exceeds specialist experience.
tasks.human_edge: Integrating evidence and experience while recognising the limits of one's competence.
tasks.altitude: No automatic specialist status or reduction in professional learning time.

reach.learn: Case selection, evidence appraisal and limits of independent practice

evidence.claim: A documentation or record-question assistant does not demonstrate veterinary specialist competence or establish reduced learning and case-practice time.

assumptions: This broad task describes specialist development and practice in one field; dentistry, pathology, nutrition, surgery, microbiology and internal medicine are alternatives. In a roll-up, specialist clinical time is an alternative classification of treatment or diagnostic work, not additional treatment volume; assign each action once.
No machine consumes an assumed competence score or specialty approval. Human study and clinical application retain full time.

Native learning access comes first. Zero upkeep because no new learning or certification process is introduced. National specialist recognition and veterinary scope requirements remain to be confirmed.
unknowns: Whether this task overlaps already counted clinical work
research_questions: How is specialty competence evidenced without double-counting ordinary clinical tasks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Critical learning40 and specialist case practice60 retain full time; this broad task cannot add duplicate clinical savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review current demand, capacity and operational concerns across the veterinary service
Direct hospital, clinic or mobile-service operations through decisions and coordination with responsible staff

tasks.design: Use existing practice records in {OTHER} and financial information in {ERP} to inform operational direction. Keep trade-offs, escalation and staff coordination with the responsible veterinarian; this broad leadership task does not supply a separate clerical baseline to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational direction combines clinical priorities, capacity, finances and staff concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational information supports management without replacing decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Competing care needs, staffing shortages and urgent changes to service capacity.
tasks.human_edge: Setting priorities and reaching workable agreements with staff.
tasks.altitude: Operational authority and leadership time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate service capacity and administrative operations
reach.learn: Clinical escalation boundaries and resource trade-offs

evidence.claim: The digest establishes no veterinary service-leadership automation; native information access alone is not a new labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is operational review and direction, not individual appointment booking, billing, rota assembly or care delivery. Hospital, clinic and mobile service are alternative contexts. Practice-manager labour is excluded and unchanged.
No machine relies on a free capacity, urgency or staffing-readiness code. The veterinarian reads original operational information in s1 with all25 hours retained.
Native reporting and access come first; no new dashboard or automated allocation is proposed without a distinct repeated assembly baseline.
Zero incremental upkeep because existing management processes continue unchanged; no work is transferred to administrators.
unknowns: Operational decision rights and practice-manager responsibilities
Whether a separate repeated administrative operation exists
research_questions: Which measured administrative activity could be changed separately from leadership and coordination?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Context review25 and leadership75 retain full time; no generic administrative fraction is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: These programme, postmortem, specialisation and operational-leadership tasks retain professional judgement and show no established new labour saving in the stated boundaries.
reach: Coordinate with nutrition specialists, pathologists, mentors and practice managers
role.ambitious_version: A veterinarian who makes programme and operational choices explicit and seeks specialist help where evidence or competence is limited.
